Direct multiplication gives S_TT=P_v, TS_T a rank-one idempotent, and both reflexive identities. G-selfadjointness of P_v forces Gv=gv; the off-diagonal entry for TS_T then forces 2g=(2−x)〈Gw,w〉 when cs≠0. This is impossible for x≥2. For x<2, G=2I−xP_v satisfies both equations, including on the two-plane's orthogonal complement. The required Rayleigh quotient ratio gives κ≥2/(2−x) for every admissible G, even if it couples w to other directions, and the displayed metric attains it. The exceptions x=1/2,1 have orthogonal products already. The exact two-dimensional witness has x=4 and an off-diagonal sign contradiction.
